items.explanation: 80-year-old woman with persistent atrial fibrillation documented in every cardiology clinic note (most recently 6/22/2026). Current medications are aspirin 81 mg and gabapentin only - no oral anticoagulant is ordered and none is active as of 9/24/2026. CHA2DS2-VASc 9 (hypertensive heart disease with heart failure 1, hypertension 1, age >=75 2, type 2 diabetes 1, prior TIA/cerebral infarction with residual hemiplegia 2, coronary atherosclerosis 1, female 1). Guideline-directed oral anticoagulation is indicated; aspirin alone is not adequate stroke prophylaxis.

Taking citalopram 40 mg daily (current order 62da0901, 7/15/2026-1/7/2027), a QT watch-list drug, and at a dose above the 20 mg maximum usually advised when QT prolongation is a concern. Her most recent ECG (104821039, 11/10/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 71 bpm with QT about 505 ms and QTc (Bazett) 542 ms, above the 500 ms review threshold. Most recent potassium 4.6 mEq/L (7/15/2026) and magnesium 2.0 mg/dL (3/8/2025) are normal, so the prolongation is not explained by electrolytes. Prescriber review of the citalopram dose and a repeat ECG are needed.

95-year-old woman taking amiodarone 200 mg daily (current order c67148bf, 6/17/2026-1/6/2027), a QT watch-list drug. Her most recent ECG (101515306, 4/27/2022) shows sinus rhythm at 58 bpm with a long QT of about 575 ms and QTc (Bazett) 561 ms, far above the 500 ms review threshold; the previous tracing three weeks earlier (100867733) was atrial fibrillation at 128 bpm with QTc 444 ms. Most recent electrolytes 6/17/2026: potassium 4.2 mEq/L, magnesium 1.9 mg/dL. Prescriber review and an up-to-date ECG are needed, particularly as she also takes warfarin and metoprolol.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (a QT watch-list drug) was started at the 3/2/2026 cardiology clinic visit; it first appears in that visit's current medication list and the order was authored the same day. Because the start was on or after 3/1/2026 the revised memo applies and an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 3/16/2026. ECG 104882441 was obtained on 3/7/2026 (5 days) and showed sinus rhythm at 81 bpm with QTc 373 ms, so the requirement was met.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily was started at the 11/10/2025 cardiology clinic visit (first appearance in the medication list; order authored that day). The start was between 9/1/2025 and 3/1/2026, so the 9/1/2025 memo applies and an ECG was required within 30 days, i.e. by 12/10/2025. ECG 106885519 was obtained on 11/24/2025 (14 days), satisfying the requirement - although it showed a QTc of 553 ms, which is flagged separately as a QT safety issue.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the 2/12/2026 cardiology clinic visit (order 0d807827 authored that day; first appearance in the medication list). Because the start was before 3/1/2026 the 30-day window of the 9/1/2025 memo applies, so an ECG was due by 3/14/2026. ECG 101538691 was obtained on 3/8/2026 (24 days) and showed sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with QTc about 448 ms, below the 500 ms review threshold. Requirement met.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the 4/10/2026 cardiology clinic visit (order ead8699a authored that day; earliest escitalopram order and earliest note for this patient). The start is on or after 3/1/2026, so the revised memo applies and an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 4/24/2026. The only ECG in the chart (107859369) was recorded on 4/29/2026, 19 days after the start and outside the required window, so the monitoring requirement was not satisfied in time and remains outstanding as of 9/24/2026.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the 8/1/2026 cardiology clinic visit (order 9fa1dfe1 authored that day; the drug first appears in that note's medication list, the 2/18/2026 note listing only aspirin and atorvastatin). Start on or after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 8/15/2026. No ECG has been recorded since 12/25/2025, so the requirement is overdue.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the 8/10/2026 cardiology clinic visit (order d7292a2a authored that day; the 3/8/2026 note listed gabapentin only). Start on or after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 8/24/2026. The 8/25/2026 telephone note records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 8/18/2026 - within the window - but the report was requested by fax and has not been received, and no tracing is in the chart. Completion therefore cannot be determined until the outside report arrives.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (a QT watch-list drug) was started at the 9/15/2026 cardiology clinic visit (order 34d26a30 authored that day). Start on or after 3/1/2026, so an ECG is required within 14 days, i.e. by 9/29/2026. No ECG has been obtained since 3/9/2025, but as of the 9/24/2026 evaluation the requirement is not yet due.

At the 9/1/2026 cardiology clinic visit the clinician documented 'INR today 1.6, subtherapeutic. Increase warfarin to 7.5 mg daily; recheck INR' - a warfarin dose change made by a Cardiology Clinic clinician after 3/1/2026, so an INR was required within 7 days, i.e. by 9/8/2026. INR 2.3 was resulted on 9/5/2026 (Observation 4282f19b), 4 days after the change, so the requirement was met.

48-year-old man with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation carried in the problem list of all cardiology clinic notes (most recently 8/4/2026). Current medications are famotidine, pantoprazole and sertraline; no anticoagulant order is active as of 9/24/2026. CHA2DS2-VASc 2 (congestive heart failure 1, hypertension 1), which meets the 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS threshold (score >=2 in men) for recommended oral anticoagulation. Needs review for initiation of a DOAC.

The 9/10/2026 anticoagulation clinic telephone note by the clinic pharmacist documents 'Home INR 3.4. Warfarin decreased from 5 mg to 4 mg daily per protocol' - a dose change made by a clinic pharmacist under the standing order, so a laboratory INR was required within 7 days, i.e. by 9/17/2026. The home INR was the trigger, not a chart result; the most recent INR in the chart is 2.7 from 6/17/2026 and no INR has been resulted since the dose change. The follow-up INR is overdue as of 9/24/2026.

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation (Condition 7010d0e5, also listed in every clinic note through 6/27/2026). Current medication list is levothyroxine only; no anticoagulant order is active as of 9/24/2026. CHA2DS2-VASc 3 (hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery 1), so anticoagulation is recommended. Remote 'hemorrhage complicating a procedure' is in the history and should be weighed, but does not by itself remove the indication.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (Condition 66dd1300). Clinic medications are famotidine, levothyroxine and metoprolol tartrate; no anticoagulant order is active as of 9/24/2026. CHA2DS2-VASc 5 (hypertension 1, prior cerebral infarction with residual left hemiparesis 2, age 65-74 1, female 1). She has already had an embolic cerebral infarction, so secondary prevention with oral anticoagulation is strongly indicated. Her 3/14/2025 ECG showed sinus rhythm with a single atrial ectopic beat, consistent with paroxysmal AF.

Apixaban 5 mg twice daily remains an active clinic order (authored 8/20/2026, valid through 1/4/2027) and is still listed as a current medication in the 8/20/2026 clinic note. However, outside records reviewed 8/12/2026 document an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer with a haemoglobin nadir of 6.9 g/dL requiring 2 units of red cells, and apixaban was explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. Continuing apixaban (plus concomitant aspirin and clopidogrel) without that documented review needs prescriber attention.

Two different oral anticoagulants are simultaneously current as of 9/24/2026: apixaban 5 mg twice daily (order 7c496afb, 7/15/2026 to 12/23/2026) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (order c4b6df94, 7/15/2026 to 1/3/2027). The 7/15/2026 clinic note states the anticoagulant was being switched from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but rivaroxaban was re-prescribed the same day and both agents are listed together in the note's current medication list. Duplicate anticoagulation markedly increases bleeding risk (he is also on clopidogrel); the rivaroxaban order should be stopped.

The 6/10/2026 cardiology clinic note records 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both 12-lead ECGs recorded that day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm with no organised P waves at a mean ventricular rate of about 134-136 bpm, i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, not sinus rhythm at 72. The documented rhythm and rate both contradict the tracings and the discrepancy needs clinical review (she carries an atrial fibrillation diagnosis and is on warfarin).

Taking escitalopram 10 mg daily (current order 438668cc, 7/18/2026-12/26/2026), a QT watch-list drug. His most recent ECG (108018814, 10/8/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with QT 494 ms and QTc (Bazett) 527 ms, at or above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring memo, so prescriber review is required. Most recent electrolytes 3/18/2026: potassium 3.8 mEq/L (low-normal) and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL. Note the 5/14/2024 clinic note recorded this tracing as 'QT acceptable', which conflicts with the measured QTc.

Taking amiodarone 200 mg daily (current order e78404bf, 7/12/2026-1/9/2027), a QT watch-list drug. His most recent ECG (106885519, 11/24/2025) shows sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with a markedly prolonged QT of about 545 ms and QTc (Bazett) 553 ms, well above the 500 ms review threshold. This is a rise of about 140 ms from the previous tracing (108780865, 6/7/2025, QTc 410 ms) after amiodarone was started on 11/10/2025. Most recent electrolytes 6/9/2026: potassium 4.3 mEq/L, magnesium 2.1 mg/dL. He is also on warfarin, which amiodarone potentiates.

interpretations.explanation: ECG 3/7/2026, the only tracing in his chart. Upright P wave in II before every QRS (0.21 mV) with a constant PR of about 184 ms; mean rate 81 bpm with gentle phasic RR variation (0.66-0.86 s) consistent with sinus arrhythmia. QRS 76 ms with normal frontal axis (+34 deg), no bundle branch block. QT 320 ms, QTc (Bazett) 373 ms - normal, which is reassuring on citalopram 40 mg. The same-day clinic note describing 'sinus rhythm' matches this tracing. No prior ECG for comparison.

ECG 7/15/2025. Sinus rhythm at 104 bpm, perfectly regular (RMSSD 5 ms), with a prominent upright P wave in II (0.22 mV) before every QRS at a PR of about 135 ms. QRS 92 ms, axis +19 deg, no conduction block. QT 335 ms, QTc (Bazett) 440 ms. Prior ECG 6/20/2025 (100698634) showed sinus tachycardia at 147 bpm with a discrete P wave (0.26 mV) and QTc 416 ms, so there is no rhythm or conduction change and the QTc change (24 ms) is below 60 ms. Despite his documented paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, both tracings are in sinus rhythm.

ECG 5/21/2024, the only tracing available. Sinus tachycardia at 108 bpm, regular, with an upright P in II preceding each QRS at a PR of about 120 ms. QRS 86 ms, frontal axis +35 deg, no bundle branch block. QT 324 ms, QTc (Bazett) 438 ms. No prior ECG for comparison.

ECG 6/10/2026 19:36. Irregularly irregular narrow-complex tachycardia at a mean ventricular rate of 136 bpm (RR 0.35-0.72 s, RMSSD 97 ms) with a fibrillating baseline and no organised P waves (beat-to-beat PQ correlation 0.13), i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response; no measurable PR interval. QRS 94 ms, frontal axis about 0 deg, no bundle branch block. QT 272 ms, QTc (Bazett) 422 ms. The earlier tracing the same day (107914094, 17:13) was also atrial fibrillation at 134 bpm with QTc 437 ms, so there is no rhythm change and the QTc change is only 15 ms. Note that the 6/10/2026 clinic note recorded 'normal sinus rhythm, rate 72', which both tracings contradict - raised as a separate documentation conflict.

ECG 8/2/2025. Regular rhythm at 69 bpm (RMSSD 7 ms) with a consistent low-amplitude atrial deflection before each QRS at a PR of about 140 ms; the P vector is unusual (negative in II, III and aVF), suggesting a low atrial/ectopic focus or limb-lead placement issue, but the rhythm is regular and atrially driven. QRS 74 ms, frontal axis -26 deg, no bundle branch block. QT 402 ms, QTc (Bazett) 431 ms. Prior ECG 4/27/2025 (104232242) was a regular atrial rhythm at 61 bpm with QRS 78 ms and QTc 399 ms but an extreme frontal axis (-174 deg, dominant negative QRS in I) consistent with reversed arm leads on that recording; the 32 ms QTc change is below 60 ms.

ECG 5/23/2024, the only tracing available. Sinus rhythm at 98 bpm, regular (RMSSD 4 ms), upright P wave in II (0.18 mV) before each QRS with a short PR of about 110 ms. QRS 72 ms, frontal axis +2 deg, no bundle branch block. QT 308 ms, QTc (Bazett) 392 ms. No prior ECG for comparison.

ECG 12/25/2025, the only tracing available. Sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, regular, with a small upright P in II before each QRS and a PR of about 145 ms. QRS 78 ms, frontal axis +20 deg, no conduction abnormality. QT 377 ms, QTc (Bazett) 412 ms - normal. This predates the escitalopram started 8/1/2026, so it does not satisfy the post-initiation ECG requirement (raised separately).

ECG 11/15/2024. Grossly irregular narrow-complex rhythm (RR 0.70-1.17 s, RMSSD 304 ms, every cycle deviating more than 10% from the median) with no P waves - the PQ segments show no beat-to-beat correlation (-0.02) and the median beat is flat before the QRS. Atrial fibrillation with a mean ventricular rate of 63 bpm; no measurable PR interval. QRS 86 ms, axis +27 deg, no bundle branch block. QT 438 ms, QTc (Bazett) 434 ms. The prior ECG of 11/12/2024 (107873952) was regular sinus rhythm at 69 bpm with a 0.23 mV P wave, PR 172 ms and QTc 398 ms, so atrial fibrillation is new; the QTc change (36 ms) is below 60 ms. She is anticoagulated with apixaban.

ECG 3/9/2025. Sinus bradycardia at 58 bpm with a clear upright P wave in II (0.18 mV) before every QRS and a PR of about 112 ms; RR variation is respiratory (RMSSD 42 ms). QRS 84 ms, frontal axis +57 deg, no bundle branch block. QT 416 ms, QTc (Bazett) 410 ms. Prior ECG 3/8/2025 (106045460) was virtually identical (sinus 62 bpm, PR 110 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc 434 ms); QTc change 24 ms, no rhythm or conduction change. This tracing predates the haloperidol started 9/15/2026.

ECG 8/23/2025, the only tracing available. Sinus rhythm at 83 bpm, regular (RMSSD 5 ms), with an upright P in II before each QRS at a PR of about 145 ms. QRS 70 ms, frontal axis +51 deg, no conduction abnormality. QT 339 ms, QTc (Bazett) 399 ms. No prior ECG for comparison.

ECG 6/19/2020. Sinus rhythm at 76 bpm, regular, with a tall upright P wave in II (0.26 mV) before each QRS and a PR of about 150 ms. QRS 70 ms, frontal axis +67 deg, no bundle branch block. QT 403 ms, QTc (Bazett) 456 ms. Prior ECG 2/2/2020 (109048192) was also sinus at 75 bpm with QRS 68 ms but had low-amplitude inverted T waves and a longer QTc of about 509 ms; the 53 ms fall is just below the 60 ms threshold, so no QTc change is flagged.

ECG 1/18/2021. Regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 120 bpm with a discrete upright P wave in II (0.20 mV) at a fixed PR of about 190 ms - sinus tachycardia. QRS 92 ms, axis +42 deg, no conduction block. QT 278 ms, QTc 393 ms. Compared with the prior ECG of 9/16/2016 (sinus tachycardia 108 bpm, PR 172 ms, QRS 88 ms, QTc 392 ms) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc (change 1 ms).

ECG 6/23/2025. Sinus bradycardia at 55 bpm, regular (RMSSD 16 ms), with an upright P in II/aVF before each QRS at a PR of about 185 ms - long-normal but under 200 ms, so no first-degree AV block. QRS 84 ms with a dominant R in V1 (0.64 mV) but no terminal R' or wide S laterally, so no right bundle branch block; frontal axis +37 deg. QT 398 ms, QTc (Bazett) 379 ms. Prior ECG 11/30/2024 (103042067) was sinus bradycardia at 51 bpm, PR about 185 ms, QRS 84 ms, QTc 362 ms - no rhythm, conduction or significant QTc change (17 ms).

ECG 9/13/2025 07:17. Irregularly irregular narrow-complex tachycardia with RR intervals from 0.31 to 0.60 s (RMSSD 133 ms, 73% of cycles deviating more than 10% from the median) and no organised atrial activity (PQ-segment correlation -0.01): atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, mean rate 147 bpm; no measurable PR interval. QRS 94 ms, frontal axis -12 deg, no bundle branch block. QT 260 ms, QTc (Bazett) 413 ms. The prior ECG of 9/12/2025 18:57 (107374881) was a regular rhythm at 77 bpm with low-amplitude but consistent P waves, so the atrial fibrillation is new; QTc essentially unchanged (415 to 413 ms). He was started on amiodarone and later apixaban after this tracing.

ECG 11/23/2025. Sinus rhythm at 72 bpm with an upright P wave in II (0.21 mV) before every QRS at a PR of about 175 ms; one slightly early beat otherwise regular. QRS 86 ms, frontal axis +10 deg, no bundle branch block. QT 349 ms, QTc (Bazett) 386 ms - now normal. The prior ECG of 11/21/2025 (105362569) was also sinus (67 bpm, PR about 155 ms, QRS 86 ms) but with QT 500 ms and QTc 530 ms, so the QTc has fallen by about 144 ms, exceeding the 60 ms threshold. The same-day clinic note documenting 'sinus rhythm' agrees with this tracing.

ECG 2/15/2025, the only tracing available. Sinus rhythm at 76 bpm with an upright P in II before each QRS at a PR of about 180 ms; RR intervals are regular apart from one early beat. QRS 90 ms, frontal axis +39 deg, no bundle branch block. QT 383 ms, QTc (Bazett) 425 ms. No prior ECG for comparison.

ECG 6/26/2023. Regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 111 bpm (RR 0.536-0.540 s) with a single discrete, tall upright P wave in II/III/aVF (0.20 mV) before each QRS at a PR of about 165 ms and an isoelectric TQ segment - sinus tachycardia, not the atrial flutter carried in his problem list (there is no second atrial wave per cycle and no sawtooth). QRS 90 ms, axis +39 deg, no bundle branch block. QT 286 ms, QTc (Bazett) 390 ms. Prior ECG 7/4/2022 (102955795) was also sinus tachycardia at 115 bpm with QRS 90 ms and QTc 381 ms - no change.

ECG 3/14/2025, the only tracing available. Underlying sinus rhythm at about 62 bpm with an upright P wave in II before each QRS at a PR of roughly 185 ms; the single short RR (0.56 s) followed by a compensatory pause (1.36 s) is a premature atrial complex, and the remaining cycles are regular at 0.96-0.99 s (so the high overall RMSSD is due to the ectopic beat, not fibrillation). QRS 96 ms, frontal axis -25 deg, no bundle branch block. QT 373 ms, QTc (Bazett) 379 ms. No prior ECG. Sinus rhythm here is compatible with her documented paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, which remains unanticoagulated (raised separately).

ECG 4/29/2026, the only tracing available. Regular rhythm at 70 bpm (RMSSD 13 ms) with a consistent atrial deflection before each QRS (upright in III, inverted in II) and a PR of about 105 ms. The frontal plane is markedly abnormal: lead I is entirely negative (S 1.4 mV) with a tall positive QRS in aVR, giving a measured frontal axis of -175 deg (extreme axis deviation), while praecordial R-wave progression V1 to V6 is normal - the pattern of reversed arm electrodes rather than true extreme axis deviation. QRS 90 ms, no bundle branch block. QT 356 ms, QTc (Bazett) 383 ms - normal on escitalopram. Repeat with correct lead placement is advised. No prior ECG for comparison.

ECG 11/10/2023. Sinus rhythm at 71 bpm, regular, with an upright P in II before each QRS at a PR of about 155 ms. QRS 94 ms, frontal axis +38 deg, no bundle branch block. The T waves are broad and late-peaking with QT about 505 ms and QTc (Bazett) 542 ms - markedly prolonged. Prior ECG 6/17/2020 (107149156) was sinus tachycardia at 132 bpm with QRS 86 ms, a rightward axis (+96 deg) and QTc 439 ms, so the QTc has increased by about 103 ms. She takes citalopram 40 mg daily, so this has been raised for QT review.

ECG 3/8/2026, the only tracing available and the study obtained after escitalopram was started on 2/12/2026. Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, regular, with an upright P wave in II (0.18 mV) before each QRS at a PR of about 150 ms. QRS 82 ms, frontal axis +56 deg, no bundle branch block. QT about 420 ms with QTc (Bazett) 448 ms - upper normal but below the 500 ms threshold that would require prescriber review. No prior ECG for comparison.

ECG 1/13/2019. Slow, somewhat irregular rhythm at a mean 53 bpm (RR 0.96-1.31 s). Five of the nine beats are preceded by a clear upright P wave in II at a constant PR of about 160 ms, while the four beats terminating the shorter cycles have no discernible P wave - sinus bradycardia with intermittent junctional escape beats rather than atrial fibrillation (P waves are definitely present and reproducible on the sinus-conducted beats). QRS 88 ms, frontal axis -9 deg, no bundle branch block. QT 388 ms, QTc (Bazett) 370 ms. Prior ECG 12/13/2018 (108651109) was regular sinus rhythm at 66 bpm with PR about 190 ms, QRS 104 ms and QTc 385 ms; no conduction or QTc change (15 ms).

ECG 10/8/2023. Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, upright P in II, PR about 140 ms, QRS 86 ms, axis +45 deg, no bundle branch block. The T waves are broad and late-peaking with QT about 495 ms and QTc (Bazett) 527 ms - markedly prolonged. The prior ECG of 11/23/2022 (100065910) was sinus at 75 bpm with QTc 352 ms, so the QTc has risen by about 175 ms, far exceeding 60 ms. He takes escitalopram, a QT watch-list drug, so this has been flagged for prescriber review.

ECG 7/13/2022. Regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 141 bpm with remarkably constant RR intervals (0.40-0.45 s, RMSSD 11 ms) and a low-amplitude but reproducible atrial deflection about 120 ms before each QRS - sinus tachycardia; there is only one atrial wave per cycle, so no flutter, and no pacing spikes despite the pacemaker in his history. QRS 82 ms, frontal axis +5 deg, no bundle branch block. QT 274 ms, QTc (Bazett) 420 ms. Prior ECG 7/11/2022 (109839112) was irregularly irregular at 110 bpm with no organised P waves (RMSSD 193 ms, PQ correlation 0.07), i.e. atrial fibrillation, so the atrial fibrillation has resolved; QTc change 18 ms.

ECG 5/12/2025, the only tracing available. Sinus rhythm at 82 bpm, regular (RMSSD 11 ms), with an upright P in II before each QRS at a PR of about 155 ms. QRS 100 ms - mildly widened but below 120 ms, with no RBBB or LBBB morphology; frontal axis +21 deg. QT 372 ms, QTc (Bazett) 435 ms. No prior ECG for comparison.

ECG 7/16/2022. Sinus rhythm at 91 bpm, regular (RMSSD 3 ms), with an upright P wave in II before each QRS at a PR of about 185 ms. QRS 80 ms, frontal axis about 0 deg, no bundle branch block. QT 333 ms, QTc (Bazett) 410 ms. Prior ECG 5/16/2021 (102616671) was sinus at 87 bpm, PR about 145 ms, QRS 80 ms, QTc 388 ms - no rhythm, conduction or significant QTc change (22 ms).

ECG 7/17/2024. Sinus rhythm at a mean 59 bpm (first two cycles longer, then regular at about 0.98 s) with an upright P in II peaking about 240 ms before the QRS and a PR of roughly 215-220 ms, i.e. first-degree AV block. QRS is broad at 130 ms with a deep QS complex in V1-V2 (V1 S 1.4 mV, no terminal R'), a broad monophasic R in I and V6 and absent septal q waves - complete left bundle branch block. Frontal axis -25 deg. QT 449 ms, QTc (Bazett) 453 ms. Prior ECG 6/3/2024 (103686933) showed the same sinus rhythm with first-degree AV block (PR about 215 ms) and LBBB (QRS 130 ms) and QTc 455 ms, so nothing has changed.

ECG 3/19/2025. Sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 102 bpm, regular (RMSSD 3 ms), with an upright P in II (0.15 mV) before each QRS at a PR of about 145 ms. QRS 86 ms, frontal axis +39 deg, no bundle branch block. QT 327 ms, QTc (Bazett) 426 ms. Prior ECG 3/18/2025 (101016166) was essentially identical (sinus 102 bpm, PR about 135 ms, QRS 82 ms, QTc 421 ms) - no change.

ECG 9/22/2025, the only tracing available. Sinus rhythm at a mean 66 bpm: an upright P wave precedes each QRS at a PR of about 155 ms, and apart from one premature beat (RR 0.754 s) with a subsequent pause (1.068 s) the cycles are regular at 0.90-0.93 s, so this is sinus rhythm with an atrial ectopic beat rather than atrial fibrillation. Low overall QRS voltage. QRS 86 ms, frontal axis -27 deg, no bundle branch block. QT 366 ms, QTc (Bazett) 383 ms. No prior ECG for comparison.

ECG 4/27/2022. Sinus rhythm at 58 bpm, essentially regular, with a small upright P wave in II/aVF before each QRS at a PR of about 180 ms. QRS 86 ms, frontal axis +23 deg, no bundle branch block. The T waves are very broad with QT about 575 ms and QTc (Bazett) 561 ms - markedly prolonged, relevant to her long-term amiodarone (raised separately for QT review). Prior ECG 4/6/2022 (100867733) was irregularly irregular at 128 bpm with no organised P waves (RMSSD 142 ms, PQ correlation 0.10), i.e. atrial fibrillation with QTc 444 ms, so atrial fibrillation has resolved and the QTc has risen by about 117 ms.

ECG 5/1/2022. Sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 107 bpm, regular (RMSSD 4 ms), with an upright P wave in II (0.21 mV) before each QRS at a PR of about 160 ms. QRS 70 ms, frontal axis +46 deg, no bundle branch block. QT 322 ms, QTc (Bazett) 430 ms. Prior ECG 7/27/2019 (107274479) was sinus at 75 bpm, PR about 155 ms, QRS 70 ms, QTc 421 ms - no rhythm, conduction or significant QTc change (9 ms).

ECG 4/19/2024, the only tracing available. Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm: regular RR (RMSSD 4 ms) with an upright P wave in II preceding each QRS at a PR of about 130 ms. QRS 80 ms, frontal axis +64 deg, no conduction abnormality. QT 302 ms with QTc (Bazett) 414 ms. No prior ECG for comparison.

ECG 8/23/2021 10:07, taken 34 seconds after the preceding tracing. Sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 102 bpm, upright P in II (0.17 mV), PR 144 ms, QRS 84 ms, axis +59 deg, no block. QT 314 ms, QTc 408 ms. Essentially identical to the immediately preceding ECG 102910502 (100 bpm, PR 144 ms, QRS 84 ms, QTc 404 ms): no rhythm, conduction or QTc change.

ECG 10/24/2024. Sinus bradycardia at 52 bpm, regular (RMSSD 10 ms), with a low-amplitude but consistent upright P wave in II and a PR of about 170 ms. QRS 90 ms, axis +34 deg, no bundle branch block; no evidence of the previously coded Mobitz II block on this tracing. QT 433 ms, QTc (Bazett) 401 ms. Prior ECG 5/22/2023 (104629882) was sinus bradycardia at 58 bpm with a single atrial ectopic beat and post-extrasystolic pause, PR 150 ms, QRS 88 ms, QTc 392 ms - no interval or rhythm change.

ECG 12/5/2024 14:38. Sinus tachycardia at 122 bpm with an upright P in II before each QRS, PR about 125 ms. The QRS has narrowed to 90 ms with no terminal R' in V1, so the right bundle branch block present earlier the same day has resolved. CHA2DS2-VASc 9 (hypertensive heart disease with heart failure 1, hypertension 1, age >=75 2, type 2 diabetes 1, prior TIA/cerebral infarction with residual hemiplegia 2, coronary atherosclerosis 1, female 1). Guideline-directed oral anticoagulation is indicated; aspirin alone is not adequate stroke prophylaxis.

Taking citalopram 40 mg daily (current order 62da0901, 7/15/2026-1/7/2027), a QT watch-list drug, and at a dose above the 20 mg maximum usually advised when QT prolongation is a concern. Her most recent ECG (104821039, 11/10/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 71 bpm with QT about 505 ms and QTc (Bazett) 542 ms, above the 500 ms review threshold. Most recent potassium 4.6 mEq/L (7/15/2026) and magnesium 2.0 mg/dL (3/8/2025) are normal, so the prolongation is not explained by electrolytes. Prescriber review of the citalopram dose and a repeat ECG are needed.

Most recent electrolytes 6/17/2026: potassium 4.2 mEq/L, magnesium 1.9 mg/dL. Prescriber review and an up-to-date ECG are needed, particularly as she also takes warfarin and metoprolol.

CHA2DS2-VASc 5 (hypertension 1, prior cerebral infarction with residual left hemiparesis 2, age 65-74 1, female 1). She has already had an embolic cerebral infarction, so secondary prevention with oral anticoagulation is strongly indicated. Her 3/14/2025 ECG showed sinus rhythm with a single atrial ectopic beat, consistent with paroxysmal AF.

Apixaban 5 mg twice daily remains an active clinic order (authored 8/20/2026, valid through 1/4/2027) and is still listed as a current medication in the 8/20/2026 clinic note. However, outside records reviewed 8/12/2026 document an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer with a haemoglobin nadir of 6.9 g/dL requiring 2 units of red cells, and apixaban was explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. Continuing apixaban (plus concomitant aspirin and clopidogrel) without that documented review needs prescriber attention.

Two different oral anticoagulants are simultaneously current as of 9/24/2026: apixaban 5 mg twice daily (order 7c496afb, 7/15/2026 to 12/23/2026) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (order c4b6df94, 7/15/2026 to 1/3/2027). The 7/15/2026 clinic note states the anticoagulant was being switched from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but rivaroxaban was re-prescribed the same day and both agents are listed together in the note's current medication list. Duplicate anticoagulation markedly increases bleeding risk (he is also on clopidogrel); the rivaroxaban order should be stopped.

The 6/10/2026 cardiology clinic note records 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both 12-lead ECGs recorded that day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm with no organised P waves at a mean ventricular rate of about 134-136 bpm, i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, not sinus rhythm at 72. The documented rhythm and rate both contradict the tracings and the discrepancy needs clinical review (she carries an atrial fibrillation diagnosis and is on warfarin).

Taking escitalopram 10 mg daily (current order 438668cc, 7/18/2026-12/26/2026), a QT watch-list drug. His most recent ECG (108018814, 10/8/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with QT 494 ms and QTc (Bazett) 527 ms, at or above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring memo, so prescriber review is required. Most recent electrolytes 3/18/2026: potassium 3.8 mEq/L (low-normal) and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL. Note the 5/14/2024 clinic note recorded this tracing as 'QT acceptable', which conflicts with the measured QTc.

Taking amiodarone 200 mg daily (current order e78404bf, 7/12/2026-1/9/2027), a QT watch-list drug. His most recent ECG (106885519, 11/24/2025) shows sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with a markedly prolonged QT of about 545 ms and QTc (Bazett) 553 ms, well above the 500 ms review threshold. This is a rise of about 140 ms from the previous tracing (108780865, 6/7/2025, QTc 410 ms) after amiodarone was started on 11/10/2025. Most recent electrolytes 6/9/2026: potassium 4.3 mEq/L, magnesium 2.1 mg/dL. He is also on warfarin, which amiodarone potentiates.

interpretations.explanation: ECG 3/7/2026, the only tracing in his chart. Upright P wave in II before every QRS (0.21 mV) with a constant PR of about 184 ms; mean rate 81 bpm with gentle phasic RR variation (0.66-0.86 s) consistent with sinus arrhythmia. QRS 76 ms with normal frontal axis (+34 deg), no bundle branch block. QT 320 ms, QTc (Bazett) 373 ms - normal, which is reassuring on citalopram 40 mg. The same-day clinic note describing 'sinus rhythm' matches this tracing. No prior ECG for comparison.

ECG 7/15/2025. Sinus rhythm at 104 bpm, perfectly regular (RMSSD 5 ms), with a prominent upright P wave in II (0.22 mV) before every QRS at a PR of about 135 ms. QRS 92 ms, axis +19 deg, no conduction block. QT 335 ms, QTc (Bazett) 440 ms. Prior ECG 6/20/2025 (100698634) showed sinus tachycardia at 147 bpm with a discrete P wave (0.26 mV) and QTc 416 ms, so there is no rhythm or conduction change and the QTc change (24 ms) is below 60 ms. Despite his documented paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, both tracings are in sinus rhythm.

ECG 5/21/2024, the only tracing available. Sinus tachycardia at 108 bpm, regular, with an upright P in II preceding each QRS at a PR of about 120 ms. QRS 86 ms, frontal axis +35 deg, no bundle branch block. QT 324 ms, QTc (Bazett) 438 ms. No prior ECG for comparison.

ECG 6/10/2026 19:36. Irregularly irregular narrow-complex tachycardia at a mean ventricular rate of 136 bpm (RR 0.35-0.72 s, RMSSD 97 ms) with a fibrillating baseline and no organised P waves (beat-to-beat PQ correlation 0.13), i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response; no measurable PR interval. QRS 94 ms, frontal axis about 0 deg, no bundle branch block. QT 272 ms, QTc (Bazett) 422 ms. The earlier tracing the same day (107914094, 17:13) was also atrial fibrillation at 134 bpm with QTc 437 ms, so there is no rhythm change and the QTc change is only 15 ms. Note that the 6/10/2026 clinic note recorded 'normal sinus rhythm, rate 72', which both tracings contradict - raised as a separate documentation conflict.

ECG 8/2/2025. Regular rhythm at 69 bpm (RMSSD 7 ms) with a consistent low-amplitude atrial deflection before each QRS at a PR of about 140 ms; the P vector is unusual (negative in II, III and aVF), suggesting a low atrial/ectopic focus or limb-lead placement issue, but the rhythm is regular and atrially driven. QRS 74 ms, frontal axis -26 deg, no bundle branch block. QT 402 ms, QTc (Bazett) 431 ms. Prior ECG 4/27/2025 (104232242) was a regular atrial rhythm at 61 bpm with QRS 78 ms and QTc 399 ms but an extreme frontal axis (-174 deg, dominant negative QRS in I) consistent with reversed arm leads on that recording; the 32 ms QTc change is below 60 ms.

ECG 5/23/2024, the only tracing available. Sinus rhythm at 98 bpm, regular (RMSSD 4 ms), upright P wave in II (0.18 mV) before each QRS with a short PR of about 110 ms. QRS 72 ms, frontal axis +2 deg, no bundle branch block. QT 308 ms, QTc (Bazett) 392 ms. No prior ECG for comparison.

ECG 12/25/2025, the only tracing available. Sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, regular, with a small upright P in II before each QRS and a PR of about 145 ms. QRS 78 ms, frontal axis +20 deg, no conduction abnormality. QT 377 ms, QTc (Bazett) 412 ms - normal. This predates the escitalopram started 8/1/2026, so it does not satisfy the post-initiation ECG requirement (raised separately).

ECG 1/18/2021. Regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 120 bpm with a discrete upright P wave in II (0.20 mV) at a fixed PR of about 190 ms - sinus tachycardia. QRS 92 ms, axis +42 deg, no conduction block. QT 278 ms, QTc 393 ms. Compared with the prior ECG of 9/16/2016 (sinus tachycardia 108 bpm, PR 172 ms, QRS 88 ms, QTc 392 ms) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc (change 1 ms).

ECG 10/8/2023. Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, upright P in II, PR about 140 ms, QRS 86 ms, axis +45 deg, no bundle branch block. The T waves are broad and late-peaking with QT about 495 ms and QTc (Bazett) 527 ms - markedly prolonged. The prior ECG of 11/23/2022 (100065910) was sinus at 75 bpm with QTc 352 ms, so the QTc has risen by about 175 ms, far exceeding 60 ms. He takes escitalopram, a QT watch-list drug, so this has been flagged for prescriber review.

ECG 4/19/2024, the only tracing available. Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm: regular RR (RMSSD 4 ms) with an upright P wave in II preceding each QRS at a PR of about 130 ms. QRS 80 ms, frontal axis +64 deg, no conduction abnormality. QT 302 ms with QTc (Bazett) 414 ms. No prior ECG for comparison.

ECG 8/23/2021 10:07, taken 34 seconds after the preceding tracing. Sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 102 bpm, upright P in II (0.17 mV), PR 144 ms, QRS 84 ms, axis +59 deg, no block. QT 314 ms, QTc 408 ms. Essentially identical to the immediately preceding ECG 102910502 (100 bpm, PR 144 ms, QRS 84 ms, QTc 404 ms): no rhythm, conduction or QTc change.

ECG 10/24/2024. Sinus bradycardia at 52 bpm, regular (RMSSD 10 ms), with a low-amplitude but consistent upright P wave in II and a PR of about 170 ms. QRS 90 ms, axis +34 deg, no bundle branch block; no evidence of the previously coded Mobitz II block on this tracing. QT 433 ms, QTc (Bazett) 401 ms. Prior ECG 5/22/2023 (104629882) was sinus bradycardia at 58 bpm with a single atrial ectopic beat and post-extrasystolic pause, PR 150 ms, QRS 88 ms, QTc 392 ms - no interval or rhythm change.

ECG 12/5/2024 14:38. Sinus tachycardia at 122 bpm with an upright P in II before each QRS, PR about 125 ms. The QRS has narrowed to 90 ms with no terminal R' in V1, so the right bundle branch block present earlier the same day has resolved. Frontal axis is rightward (+106 deg) with an rS pattern in I and V6. QT 293 ms, QTc 418 ms. Prior ECG 106516875 (12/5/2024 01:33) showed sinus rhythm at 100 bpm with QRS 142 ms, a tall terminal R in V1 (1.1 mV) and wide S waves in I and V6, i.e. complete RBBB, with QTc 461 ms; the 43 ms QTc fall is below the 60 ms threshold.

ECG 11/24/2025. Sinus rhythm at 62 bpm, regular, with a small upright P wave in II/III/aVF and a PR of roughly 160-170 ms (below the 200 ms threshold, so no first-degree AV block). QRS 96 ms, axis +46 deg, no bundle branch block. The T waves are very broad and low with QT about 545 ms and QTc (Bazett) 553 ms - markedly prolonged. Prior ECG 6/7/2025 (108780865) was sinus bradycardia at 49 bpm with QTc 410 ms, so the QTc has risen about 143 ms after amiodarone was started on 11/10/2025; flagged separately for QT review.

ECG 9/17/2024, the only tracing available. Irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm (RR 0.41-1.07 s, RMSSD 256 ms, 60% of cycles deviating more than 10% from the median) with no organised P waves anywhere - the median beat is flat throughout the PQ interval and beat-to-beat PQ-segment correlation is only 0.18. This is atrial fibrillation with a mean ventricular rate of 103 bpm; no measurable PR interval. QRS 76 ms, frontal axis -44 deg (left axis deviation), no bundle branch block. QT 317 ms, QTc (Bazett) 413 ms. No prior ECG for comparison. He carries an atrial fibrillation diagnosis and is anticoagulated with warfarin.

Despite his documented paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, both tracings are in sinus rhythm.

CHA2DS2-VASc 9 (hypertensive heart disease with heart failure 1, hypertension 1, age >=75 2, type 2 diabetes 1, prior TIA/cerebral infarction with residual hemiplegia 2, coronary atherosclerosis 1, female 1). Guideline-directed oral anticoagulation is indicated; aspirin alone is not adequate stroke prophylaxis.

Taking citalopram 40 mg daily (current order 62da0901, 7/15/2026-1/7/2027), a QT watch-list drug, and at a dose above the 20 mg maximum usually advised when QT prolongation is a concern. Her most recent ECG (104821039, 11/10/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 71 bpm with QT about 505 ms and QTc (Bazett) 542 ms, above the 500 ms review threshold. Most recent potassium 4.6 mEq/L (7/15/2026) and magnesium 2.0 mg/dL (3/8/2025) are normal, so the prolongation is not explained by electrolytes. Prescriber review of the citalopram dose and a repeat ECG are needed.

95-year-old woman taking amiodarone 200 mg daily (current order c67148bf, 6/17/2026-1/6/2027), a QT watch-list drug. Her most recent ECG (101515306, 4/27/2022) shows sinus rhythm at 58 bpm with a long QT of about 575 ms and QTc (Bazett) 561 ms, far above the 500 ms review threshold; the previous tracing three weeks earlier (100867733) was atrial fibrillation at 128 bpm with QTc 444 ms. Most recent electrolytes 6/17/2026: potassium 4.2 mEq/L, magnesium 1.9 mg/dL. Prescriber review and an up-to-date ECG are needed, particularly as she also takes warfarin and metoprolol.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (a QT watch-list drug) was started at the 3/2/2026 cardiology clinic visit; it first appears in that visit's current medication list and the order was authored the same day. Because the start was on or after 3/1/2026 the revised memo applies and an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 3/16/2026. ECG 104882441 was obtained on 3/7/2026 (5 days) and showed sinus rhythm at 81 bpm with QTc 373 ms, so the requirement was met.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily was started at the 11/10/2025 cardiology clinic visit (first appearance in the medication list; order authored that day). The start was between 9/1/2025 and 3/1/2026, so the 9/1/2025 memo applies and an ECG was required within 30 days, i.e. by 12/10/2025. ECG 106885519 was obtained on 11/24/2025 (14 days), satisfying the requirement - although it showed a QTc of 553 ms, which is flagged separately as a QT safety issue.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the 2/12/2026 cardiology clinic visit (order 0d807827 authored that day; first appearance in the medication list). Because the start was before 3/1/2026 the 30-day window of the 9/1/2025 memo applies, so an ECG was due by 3/14/2026. ECG 101538691 was obtained on 3/8/2026 (24 days) and showed sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with QTc about 448 ms, below the 500 ms review threshold. Requirement met.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the 4/10/2026 cardiology clinic visit (order ead8699a authored that day; earliest escitalopram order and earliest note for this patient). The start is on or after 3/1/2026, so the revised memo applies and an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 4/24/2026. The only ECG in the chart (107859369) was recorded on 4/29/2026, 19 days after the start and outside the required window, so the monitoring requirement was not satisfied in time and remains outstanding as of 9/24/2026.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the 8/1/2026 cardiology clinic visit (order 9fa1dfe1 authored that day; the drug first appears in that note's medication list, the 2/18/2026 note listing only aspirin and atorvastatin). Start on or after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 8/15/2026. No ECG has been recorded since 12/25/2025, so the requirement is overdue.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the 8/10/2026 cardiology clinic visit (order d7292a2a authored that day; the 3/8/2026 note listed gabapentin only). Start on or after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 8/24/2026. The 8/25/2026 telephone note records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 8/18/2026 - within the window - but the report was requested by fax and has not been received, and no tracing is in the chart. Completion therefore cannot be determined until the outside report arrives.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (a QT watch-list drug) was started at the 9/15/2026 cardiology clinic visit (order 34d26a30 authored that day). Start on or after 3/1/2026, so an ECG is required within 14 days, i.e. by 9/29/2026. No ECG has been obtained since 3/9/2025, but as of the 9/24/2026 evaluation the requirement is not yet due.

At the 9/1/2026 cardiology clinic visit the clinician documented 'INR today 1.6, subtherapeutic. Increase warfarin to 7.5 mg daily; recheck INR' - a warfarin dose change made by a Cardiology Clinic clinician after 3/1/2026, so an INR was required within 7 days, i.e. by 9/8/2026. INR 2.3 was resulted on 9/5/2026 (Observation 4282f19b), 4 days after the change, so the requirement was met.

48-year-old man with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation carried in the problem list of all cardiology clinic notes (most recently 8/4/2026). Current medications are famotidine, pantoprazole and sertraline; no anticoagulant order is active as of 9/24/2026. CHA2DS2-VASc 2 (congestive heart failure 1, hypertension 1), which meets the 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS threshold (score >=2 in men) for recommended oral anticoagulation. Needs review for initiation of a DOAC.

The 9/10/2026 anticoagulation clinic telephone note by the clinic pharmacist documents 'Home INR 3.4. Warfarin decreased from 5 mg to 4 mg daily per protocol' - a dose change made by a clinic pharmacist under the standing order, so a laboratory INR was required within 7 days, i.e. by 9/17/2026. The home INR was the trigger, not a chart result; the most recent INR in the chart is 2.7 from 6/17/2026 and no INR has been resulted since the dose change. The follow-up INR is overdue as of 9/24/2026.

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation (Condition 7010d0e5, also listed in every clinic note through 6/27/2026). Current medication list is levothyroxine only; no anticoagulant order is active as of 9/24/2026. CHA2DS2-VASc 3 (hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery 1), so anticoagulation is recommended. Remote 'hemorrhage complicating a procedure' is in the history and should be weighed, but does not by itself remove the indication.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (Condition 66dd1300). Clinic medications are famotidine, levothyroxine and metoprolol tartrate; no anticoagulant order is active as of 9/24/2026. CHA2DS2-VASc 5 (hypertension 1, prior cerebral infarction with residual left hemiparesis 2, age 65-74 1, female 1). She has already had an embolic cerebral infarction, so secondary prevention with oral anticoagulation is strongly indicated. Her 3/14/2025 ECG showed sinus rhythm with a single atrial ectopic beat, consistent with paroxysmal AF.

Apixaban 5 mg twice daily remains an active clinic order (authored 8/20/2026, valid through 1/4/2027) and is still listed as a current medication in the 8/20/2026 clinic note. However, outside records reviewed 8/12/2026 document an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer with a haemoglobin nadir of 6.9 g/dL requiring 2 units of red cells, and apixaban was explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. Continuing apixaban (plus concomitant aspirin and clopidogrel) without that documented review needs prescriber attention.

Two different oral anticoagulants are simultaneously current as of 9/24/2026: apixaban 5 mg twice daily (order 7c496afb, 7/15/2026 to 12/23/2026) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (order c4b6df94, 7/15/2026 to 1/3/2027). The 7/15/2026 clinic note states the anticoagulant was being switched from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but rivaroxaban was re-prescribed the same day and both agents are listed together in the note's current medication list. Duplicate anticoagulation markedly increases bleeding risk (he is also on clopidogrel); the rivaroxaban order should be stopped.

The 6/10/2026 cardiology clinic note records 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both 12-lead ECGs recorded that day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm with no organised P waves at a mean ventricular rate of about 134-136 bpm, i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, not sinus rhythm at 72. The documented rhythm and rate both contradict the tracings and the discrepancy needs clinical review (she carries an atrial fibrillation diagnosis and is on warfarin).

Taking escitalopram 10 mg daily (current order 438668cc, 7/18/2026-12/26/2026), a QT watch-list drug. His most recent ECG (108018814, 10/8/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with QT 494 ms and QTc (Bazett) 527 ms, at or above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring memo, so prescriber review is required. Most recent electrolytes 3/18/2026: potassium 3.8 mEq/L (low-normal) and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL. Note the 5/14/2024 clinic note recorded this tracing as 'QT acceptable', which conflicts with the measured QTc.

Taking amiodarone 200 mg daily (current order e78404bf, 7/12/2026-1/9/2027), a QT watch-list drug. His most recent ECG (106885519, 11/24/2025) shows sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with a markedly prolonged QT of about 545 ms and QTc (Bazett) 553 ms, well above the 500 ms review threshold. This is a rise of about 140 ms from the previous tracing (108780865, 6/7/2025, QTc 410 ms) after amiodarone was started on 11/10/2025. Most recent electrolytes 6/9/2026: potassium 4.3 mEq/L, magnesium 2.1 mg/dL. He is also on warfarin, which amiodarone potentiates.

interpretations.explanation: ECG 3/7/2026, the only tracing in his chart. Upright P wave in II before every QRS (0.21 mV) with a constant PR of about 184 ms; mean rate 81 bpm with gentle phasic RR variation (0.66-0.86 s) consistent with sinus arrhythmia. QRS 76 ms with normal frontal axis (+34 deg), no bundle branch block. QT 320 ms, QTc (Bazett) 373 ms - normal, which is reassuring on citalopram 40 mg. The same-day clinic note describing 'sinus rhythm' matches this tracing. No prior ECG for comparison.

ECG 7/15/2025. Sinus rhythm at 104 bpm, perfectly regular (RMSSD 5 ms), with a prominent upright P wave in II (0.22 mV) before every QRS at a PR of about 135 ms. QRS 92 ms, axis +19 deg, no conduction block. QT 335 ms, QTc (Bazett) 440 ms. Prior ECG 6/20/2025 (100698634) showed sinus tachycardia at 147 bpm with a discrete P wave (0.26 mV) and QTc 416 ms, so there is no rhythm or conduction change and the QTc change (24 ms) is below 60 ms. Despite his documented paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, both tracings are in sinus rhythm.

ECG 5/21/2024, the only tracing available. Sinus tachycardia at 108 bpm, regular, with an upright P in II preceding each QRS at a PR of about 120 ms. QRS 86 ms, frontal axis +35 deg, no bundle branch block. QT 324 ms, QTc (Bazett) 438 ms. No prior ECG for comparison.

ECG 6/10/2026 19:36. Irregularly irregular narrow-complex tachycardia at a mean ventricular rate of 136 bpm (RR 0.35-0.72 s, RMSSD 97 ms) with a fibrillating baseline and no organised P waves (beat-to-beat PQ correlation 0.13), i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response; no measurable PR interval. QRS 94 ms, frontal axis about 0 deg, no bundle branch block. QT 272 ms, QTc (Bazett) 422 ms. The earlier tracing the same day (107914094, 17:13) was also atrial fibrillation at 134 bpm with QTc 437 ms, so there is no rhythm change and the QTc change is only 15 ms. Note that the 6/10/2026 clinic note recorded 'normal sinus rhythm, rate 72', which both tracings contradict - raised as a separate documentation conflict.

ECG 8/2/2025. Regular rhythm at 69 bpm (RMSSD 7 ms) with a consistent low-amplitude atrial deflection before each QRS at a PR of about 140 ms; the P vector is unusual (negative in II, III and aVF), suggesting a low atrial/ectopic focus or limb-lead placement issue, but the rhythm is regular and atrially driven. QRS 74 ms, frontal axis -26 deg, no bundle branch block. QT 402 ms, QTc (Bazett) 431 ms. Prior ECG 4/27/2025 (104232242) was a regular atrial rhythm at 61 bpm with QRS 78 ms and QTc 399 ms but an extreme frontal axis (-174 deg, dominant negative QRS in I) consistent with reversed arm leads on that recording; the 32 ms QTc change is below 60 ms.

ECG 5/23/2024, the only tracing available. Sinus rhythm at 98 bpm, regular (RMSSD 4 ms), upright P wave in II (0.18 mV) before each QRS with a short PR of about 110 ms. QRS 72 ms, frontal axis +2 deg, no bundle branch block. QT 308 ms, QTc (Bazett) 392 ms. No prior ECG for comparison.

ECG 12/25/2025, the only tracing available. Sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, regular, with a small upright P in II before each QRS and a PR of about 145 ms. QRS 78 ms, frontal axis +20 deg, no conduction abnormality. QT 377 ms, QTc (Bazett) 412 ms - normal. This predates the escitalopram started 8/1/2026, so it does not satisfy the post-initiation ECG requirement (raised separately).

ECG 11/15/2024. Grossly irregular narrow-complex rhythm (RR 0.70-1.17 s, RMSSD 304 ms, every cycle deviating more than 10% from the median) with no P waves - the PQ segments show no beat-to-beat correlation (-0.02) and the median beat is flat before the QRS. Atrial fibrillation with a mean ventricular rate of 63 bpm; no measurable PR interval. QRS 86 ms, axis +27 deg, no bundle branch block. QT 438 ms, QTc (Bazett) 434 ms. The prior ECG of 11/12/2024 (107873952) was regular sinus rhythm at 69 bpm with a 0.23 mV P wave, PR 172 ms and QTc 398 ms, so atrial fibrillation is new; the QTc change (36 ms) is below 60 ms. She is anticoagulated with apixaban.

ECG 3/9/2025. Sinus bradycardia at 58 bpm with a clear upright P wave in II (0.18 mV) before every QRS and a PR of about 112 ms; RR variation is respiratory (RMSSD 42 ms). QRS 84 ms, frontal axis +57 deg, no bundle branch block. QT 416 ms, QTc (Bazett) 410 ms. Prior ECG 3/8/2025 (106045460) was virtually identical (sinus 62 bpm, PR 110 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc 434 ms); QTc change 24 ms, no rhythm or conduction change. This tracing predates the haloperidol started 9/15/2026.

ECG 8/23/2025, the only tracing available. Sinus rhythm at 83 bpm, regular (RMSSD 5 ms), with an upright P in II before each QRS at a PR of about 145 ms. QRS 70 ms, frontal axis +51 deg, no conduction abnormality. QT 339 ms, QTc (Bazett) 399 ms. No prior ECG for comparison.

ECG 6/19/2020. Sinus rhythm at 76 bpm, regular, with a tall upright P wave in II (0.26 mV) before each QRS and a PR of about 150 ms. QRS 70 ms, frontal axis +67 deg, no bundle branch block. QT 403 ms, QTc (Bazett) 456 ms. Prior ECG 2/2/2020 (109048192) was also sinus at 75 bpm with QRS 68 ms but had low-amplitude inverted T waves and a longer QTc of about 509 ms; the 53 ms fall is just below the 60 ms threshold, so no QTc change is flagged.

ECG 1/18/2021. Regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 120 bpm with a discrete upright P wave in II (0.20 mV) at a fixed PR of about 190 ms - sinus tachycardia. QRS 92 ms, axis +42 deg, no conduction block. QT 278 ms, QTc 393 ms. Compared with the prior ECG of 9/16/2016 (sinus tachycardia 108 bpm, PR 172 ms, QRS 88 ms, QTc 392 ms) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc (change 1 ms).

ECG 6/23/2025. Sinus bradycardia at 55 bpm, regular (RMSSD 16 ms), with an upright P in II/aVF before each QRS at a PR of about 185 ms - long-normal but under 200 ms, so no first-degree AV block. QRS 84 ms with a dominant R in V1 (0.64 mV) but no terminal R' or wide S laterally, so no right bundle branch block; frontal axis +37 deg. QT 398 ms, QTc (Bazett) 379 ms. Prior ECG 11/30/2024 (103042067) was sinus bradycardia at 51 bpm, PR about 185 ms, QRS 84 ms, QTc 362 ms - no rhythm, conduction or significant QTc change (17 ms).

ECG 9/13/2025 07:17. Irregularly irregular narrow-complex tachycardia with RR intervals from 0.31 to 0.60 s (RMSSD 133 ms, 73% of cycles deviating more than 10% from the median) and no organised atrial activity (PQ-segment correlation -0.01): atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, mean rate 147 bpm; no measurable PR interval. QRS 94 ms, frontal axis -12 deg, no bundle branch block. QT 260 ms, QTc (Bazett) 413 ms. The prior ECG of 9/12/2025 18:57 (107374881) was a regular rhythm at 77 bpm with low-amplitude but consistent P waves, so the atrial fibrillation is new; QTc essentially unchanged (415 to 413 ms). He was started on amiodarone and later apixaban after this tracing.

ECG 11/23/2025. Sinus rhythm at 72 bpm with an upright P wave in II (0.21 mV) before every QRS at a PR of about 175 ms; one slightly early beat otherwise regular. QRS 86 ms, frontal axis +10 deg, no bundle branch block. QT 349 ms, QTc (Bazett) 386 ms - now normal. The prior ECG of 11/21/2025 (105362569) was also sinus (67 bpm, PR about 155 ms, QRS 86 ms) but with QT 500 ms and QTc 530 ms, so the QTc has fallen by about 144 ms, exceeding the 60 ms threshold. The same-day clinic note documenting 'sinus rhythm' agrees with this tracing.

ECG 2/15/2025, the only tracing available. Sinus rhythm at 76 bpm with an upright P in II before each QRS at a PR of about 180 ms; RR intervals are regular apart from one early beat. QRS 90 ms, frontal axis +39 deg, no bundle branch block. QT 383 ms, QTc (Bazett) 425 ms. No prior ECG for comparison.

ECG 6/26/2023. Regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 111 bpm (RR 0.536-0.540 s) with a single discrete, tall upright P wave in II/III/aVF (0.20 mV) before each QRS at a PR of about 165 ms and an isoelectric TQ segment - sinus tachycardia, not the atrial flutter carried in his problem list (there is no second atrial wave per cycle and no sawtooth). QRS 90 ms, axis +39 deg, no bundle branch block. QT 286 ms, QTc (Bazett) 390 ms. Prior ECG 7/4/2022 (102955795) was also sinus tachycardia at 115 bpm with QRS 90 ms and QTc 381 ms - no change.

ECG 10/8/2023. Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, upright P in II, PR about 140 ms, QRS 86 ms, axis +45 deg, no bundle branch block. The T waves are broad and late-peaking with QT about 495 ms and QTc (Bazett) 527 ms - markedly prolonged. The prior ECG of 11/23/2022 (100065910) was sinus at 75 bpm with QTc 352 ms, so the QTc has risen by about 175 ms, far exceeding 60 ms. He takes escitalopram, a QT watch-list drug, so this has been flagged for prescriber review.

ECG 4/19/2024, the only tracing available. Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm: regular RR (RMSSD 4 ms) with an upright P wave in II preceding each QRS at a PR of about 130 ms. QRS 80 ms, frontal axis +64 deg, no conduction abnormality. QT 302 ms with QTc (Bazett) 414 ms. No prior ECG for comparison.

ECG 8/23/2021 10:07, taken 34 seconds after the preceding tracing. Sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 102 bpm, upright P in II (0.17 mV), PR 144 ms, QRS 84 ms, axis +59 deg, no block. QT 314 ms, QTc 408 ms. Essentially identical to the immediately preceding ECG 102910502 (100 bpm, PR 144 ms, QRS 84 ms, QTc 404 ms): no rhythm, conduction or QTc change.

ECG 10/24/2024. Sinus bradycardia at 52 bpm, regular (RMSSD 10 ms), with a low-amplitude but consistent upright P wave in II and a PR of about 170 ms. QRS 90 ms, axis +34 deg, no bundle branch block; no evidence of the previously coded Mobitz II block on this tracing. QT 433 ms, QTc (Bazett) 401 ms. Prior ECG 5/22/2023 (104629882) was sinus bradycardia at 58 bpm with a single atrial ectopic beat and post-extrasystolic pause, PR 150 ms, QRS 88 ms, QTc 392 ms - no interval or rhythm change.

ECG 12/5/2024 14:38. Sinus tachycardia at 122 bpm with an upright P in II before each QRS, PR about 125 ms. The QRS has narrowed to 90 ms with no terminal R' in V1, so the right bundle branch block present earlier the same day has resolved. Frontal axis is rightward (+106 deg) with an rS pattern in I and V6. QT 293 ms, QTc 418 ms. Prior ECG 106516875 (12/5/2024 01:33) showed sinus rhythm at 100 bpm with QRS 142 ms, a tall terminal R in V1 (1.1 mV) and wide S waves in I and V6, i.e. complete RBBB, with QTc 461 ms; the 43 ms QTc fall is below the 60 ms threshold.

ECG 11/24/2025. Sinus rhythm at 62 bpm, regular, with a small upright P wave in II/III/aVF and a PR of roughly 160-170 ms (below the 200 ms threshold, so no first-degree AV block). QRS 96 ms, axis +46 deg, no bundle branch block. The T waves are very broad and low with QT about 545 ms and QTc (Bazett) 553 ms - markedly prolonged. Prior ECG 6/7/2025 (108780865) was sinus bradycardia at 49 bpm with QTc 410 ms, so the QTc has risen about 143 ms after amiodarone was started on 11/10/2025; flagged separately for QT review.

ECG 9/17/2024, the only tracing available. Irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm (RR 0.41-1.07 s, RMSSD 256 ms, 60% of cycles deviating more than 10% from the median) with no organised P waves anywhere - the median beat is flat throughout the PQ interval and beat-to-beat PQ-segment correlation is only 0.18. This is atrial fibrillation with a mean ventricular rate of 103 bpm; no measurable PR interval. QRS 76 ms, frontal axis -44 deg (left axis deviation), no bundle branch block. QT 317 ms, QTc (Bazett) 413 ms. No prior ECG for comparison. He carries an atrial fibrillation diagnosis and is anticoagulated with warfarin.
